title: Cokernel of an inclusion between represented subobjects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $A,A',B,M$ be objects, let $f:A\to M$ and $g:B\to M$ be monomorphisms, let $\alpha:A\xrightarrow{\sim}A'$ be an isomorphism, and let $\phi:A'\to B$ satisfy $f=g\circ\phi\circ\alpha$. A subobject of $M$ means an isomorphism class of monomorphisms into $M$; write $[f]$ and $[g]$ for the classes represented by $f$ and $g$. Order subobjects by factorization of their monomorphisms. For any proof $h:[f]\le[g]$, let $\iota_h:\underline{[f]}\to\underline{[g]}$ be the unique map between the chosen representatives whose composite with the representative inclusion into $M$ is the inclusion of $[f]$. Then
$$\operatorname{coker}(\iota_h)\cong\operatorname{coker}(\phi).$$
Here the cokernel of a map $t:U\to V$ is the universal map $q:V\to Q$ with $q\circ t=0$. No strictness or nonzero-object hypothesis is imposed.
